providers.name: Tender Radar

pricing.plansText: Monthly pricing shown as Starter €79/month and Professional €149/month; Enterprise is custom. The annual toggle says it saves two months, but the reviewed page did not expose separate annual totals.
pricing.seatDetail: User or seat allowances are not publicly stated. Plans instead limit company profiles: 1 on Starter, up to 10 on Professional and unlimited on Enterprise.
pricing.vatDetail: Prices exclude applicable VAT or other taxes, which are added where required.
pricing.trialDetail: All paid plans advertise a free trial with no credit card required, but the duration is not stated. The service was also advertising a closed beta and waitlist ahead of public launch.

comparablePlans.includedUsers: Not publicly stated; includes 1 company profile
comparablePlans.notes: Annual toggle says Save 2 months but no annual total is published. Prices exclude applicable VAT. Join Waitlist was the active call to action.

comparablePlans.includedUsers: Not publicly stated; includes up to 10 company profiles
comparablePlans.notes: Annual toggle says Save 2 months but no annual total is published. Prices exclude applicable VAT. Join Waitlist was the active call to action.

comparablePlans.includedUsers: Not publicly stated; includes unlimited company profiles
comparablePlans.notes: Custom price; advertised API access conflicts with the roadmap's Coming Soon REST API item.

semanticAiMatching.detail: AI builds capability profiles from company websites and semantically scores tenders with an explanation of fit.

buyerProfiles.detail: Public category pages show buyer counts, but the reviewed pages do not establish structured buyer profiles.

supplierProfiles.detail: Company capability profiles are the customer's own matching configurations, not supplier, incumbent or competitor profiles.

renewalSignals.detail: Public CPV category pages display category-level re-tender likelihood, but no contract-specific expiry or renewal monitoring was established.

similarContracts.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish similar historical contracts surfaced against a notice or profile.

buyerDocuments.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish buyer plans, strategies, minutes, budgets or other buyer-authored material beyond procurement documents.

buyerRequirements.detail: Professional includes Document AI summaries, and the shipped roadmap item says uploaded documents yield requirements, deadlines and evaluation criteria. The complete capability is plan-limited to Professional and above.

requirementsPlanning.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish readiness, evidence-gap or requirements-planning workflow.

awardHistory.detail: Public CPV pages report notice history and awarded-contract counts, but no dedicated award-history search or winner-intelligence feature was established.

frameworks.detail: Tender Radar says it flags DPS opportunities and both initial framework notices and call-off notices.

competitorTracking.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish named competitor, incumbent, supplier or winner monitoring.

exportsApi.detail: Enterprise advertises API access, but the roadmap separately labels REST API access as coming soon; customer availability is therefore unclear.

collaboration.detail: The shipped roadmap describes multi-tenant workspaces with role-based access, multiple profiles and shared opportunity feeds; Professional also advertises Slack alerts.

bidWriting.detail: Tender response drafting is explicitly listed as coming soon rather than shipped.

explicitPortals.detail: Listed in the pricing coverage FAQ as a monitored UK source; current public CPV pages also identify contracts_finder in source counts.
Current public CPV pages explicitly identify find_a_tender as a source, although the coverage FAQ does not list it among the 14 monitored sources.
Coverage page names TED as the EU-wide official-journal source.
Named as an EU-wide European Commission source.
Named as a dedicated French national-portal integration.
Named as a dedicated German national-portal integration.
Named as a dedicated Spanish national-portal integration.
Named as an Italian procurement source using its open API.
Named as a dedicated Dutch national-portal integration.
Named as a dedicated Finnish national-portal integration.
Named as a dedicated Portuguese national-portal integration.
Named as a dedicated Portuguese official-gazette integration.
Named as a monitored international United Nations procurement portal.
Named as a monitored United States federal procurement source.
Named in the pricing coverage FAQ as a monitored source.
Named in the pricing coverage FAQ as a monitored source.
Named in the pricing coverage FAQ as a monitored source.

otherCoverageClaims.claim: Pricing says every plan includes all portal coverage and the coverage page says 14 data sources across 27 countries, with seven countries having dedicated national scrapers plus TED.

deepAudit.researchSummary: Tender Radar sells AI-ranked, multi-country tender discovery built from a website-derived capability profile, with document extraction and team functionality on higher plans. Its clearest depth is a named European and international source-estate plus unusually specific AI-processing and security documentation, but the commercial product still shows launch-stage inconsistencies.

legalAndMaturity.detail: The April 2026 terms choose Dutch law and Amsterdam courts, and the privacy policy names Tender Radar as controller, but neither reviewed legal page gives a registered legal entity, company number or physical address. The waitlist page describes a closed beta and summer 2026 public launch while current pricing and trial language are already published.

targetCustomerAndUseCase.detail: The service is explicitly for business professionals in procurement, sales and business development. Starter targets small businesses, Professional targets growing companies bidding across multiple fronts, and Enterprise targets organisations needing unlimited profiles, SSO and integrations.

dataSourcesAndCoverageMethod.detail: Pricing names 14 active sources spanning EU Funding & Tenders, national European portals, Contracts Finder, the Council of Europe, NATO bodies, UNGM and SAM.gov. Coverage documentation describes seven fully covered countries, dedicated national integrations plus TED, while the public product claims broader coverage across 27 countries; the provider warns that coverage is not guaranteed exhaustive.

dataIngestionAndFreshness.detail: Tender Radar says automated crawlers monitor portals around the clock, collect notices as they publish and pass them through AI classification and matching. No source-by-source polling interval, ingestion-lag report, status history or contractual freshness SLA was found.

matchingAndQualificationMethod.detail: The platform scans a customer's website into a capability profile covering services, sectors, certifications and experience, then uses OpenAI and Anthropic-backed classification to score and explain each tender's fit. AI outputs are expressly advisory and customers are told to verify tender information independently.

buyerEntityInvestment.detail: Public CPV pages expose distinct-buyer counts and buyer names on notices, but the reviewed sources do not document canonical buyer entities, aliases, duplicate merging or cross-notice buyer profiles.

supplierEntityInvestment.detail: Company profiles are customer-owned matching configurations. No canonical supplier, incumbent or winner entities, supplier aliases, or cross-award supplier intelligence were established.

renewalSignalMethod.detail: Public CPV category pages label a broad re-tender likelihood based on how often contracts in that category return. No contract-specific end-date calculation, extension evidence, incumbent expiry alert, predicted re-procurement date or confirmed future notice workflow was documented.

requirementsPlanningMethod.detail: Document AI can extract requirements, deadlines and evaluation criteria, and bid/no-bid recommendations are in progress, but no durable requirement register with evidence needs, owners, actions, dates or readiness state was found.

historicalAndAwardDepth.detail: Starter, Professional and Enterprise advertise 7-day, 90-day and unlimited match history respectively. Public category pages show all-time notice totals and award counts, but the reviewed product pages do not establish a dedicated award search with winners, award values and linked notice histories.

workflowAndIntegrations.detail: Shipped functionality includes multi-tenant workspaces, role-based access, multiple profiles and shared feeds; Professional adds Slack alerts and Enterprise advertises API access plus SSO/SAML. The roadmap still calls REST API access coming soon, so the exact currently usable API boundary needs confirmation.

securitySupportAndOnboarding.detail: The privacy policy documents EU-primary storage, named sub-processors, TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at rest, row-level multi-tenant isolation, bcrypt password hashing, access controls and retention periods. Setup is marketed as under five minutes; Professional includes priority support, Enterprise a dedicated account manager, and the contact page promises a 24-hour response during CET business hours. No independent certification, penetration-test report or public status page was found.

commercialModel.detail: The public offer is €79 per month for one-profile Starter, €149 per month for Professional with up to ten profiles, and custom Enterprise. Every plan claims all monitored portals; the 14-day trial requires a card, prices exclude VAT, and terms allow monthly or annual billing although public annual totals were not extractable from the reviewed pricing state.

materialLimitations.detail: The legal pages do not disclose a registered entity name, company or chamber number, or physical business address.
The provider expressly disclaims exhaustive portal coverage, timeliness and AI accuracy, so source completeness and match quality require trial validation.
Buyer/supplier entity intelligence, contract-specific renewals and a durable requirements-readiness workflow were not established on reviewed pages.

contradictions.detail: The waitlist describes a closed beta and summer 2026 public launch, while pricing advertises paid plans and a 14-day card-backed trial but still routes plan CTAs to Join Waitlist.
Enterprise pricing says API access is included, while the product roadmap lists REST API access as coming soon.
Pricing names Contracts Finder as active and public pages show UK records, while the roadmap describes dedicated UK coverage as coming soon.
Current first-party pages report different source totals: the About page says 13 sources, pricing says 14 active sources, and public CPV pages market monitoring across 15+ portals.

diligenceQuestions: What is the contracting legal entity, registration number and business address?
Is the product generally available now, and which trial or paid-plan functions are live rather than beta?
Which exact sources are production-active today, with source-specific polling intervals and measured ingestion lag?
What API endpoints and limits are live today, and why does the roadmap still call REST API access coming soon?
Can the provider supply a representative recall-and-precision evaluation for our categories and countries?
Are ISO 27001, SOC 2, penetration-test summaries, DPA and sub-processor change terms available for diligence?

caveats: Provider claims only; Civensa has not independently tested coverage, matching or alert delivery.
The waitlist page described Tender Radar as a closed beta with a summer 2026 public launch, and pricing calls to action still said Join Waitlist on the reviewed date.
Provider pages conflict on UK readiness: pricing lists Contracts Finder as monitored, public CPV pages show UK source data, while the roadmap still labels dedicated UK coverage as coming soon.
Enterprise pricing advertises API access while the roadmap separately lists REST API access as coming soon.

providers.name: TenderAI

pricing.plansText: £99/month per business profile with unlimited opportunities. A free weekly digest is also advertised.
pricing.seatDetail: One business profile is included; user or seat limits are not publicly stated.
pricing.vatDetail: VAT treatment is not publicly stated on the reviewed page.
pricing.trialDetail: First month free and cancel anytime. The page says no card is charged for 30 days, but does not clearly state whether a card is required for the paid-plan trial; the separate weekly digest says no credit card is needed.

comparablePlans.notes: Free weekly digest; no credit card required. This is a digest rather than the personalised daily paid profile.

comparablePlans.includedUsers: Not publicly stated; one business profile
comparablePlans.notes: The page publishes no formal plan name and prices per profile. First month is free; annual billing and VAT treatment are not published.

semanticAiMatching.detail: Every tender is scored 0-100 against a personalised business profile using claimed semantic understanding, with BID, FLAG or SKIP rationale.

buyerProfiles.detail: Buyer names appear in briefs, but the reviewed pages do not establish structured buyer-intelligence profiles.

supplierProfiles.detail: The customer's own business profile does not establish supplier, incumbent, winner or competitor profiles.

renewalSignals.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish contract expiry, renewal, extension or re-tender monitoring.

similarContracts.detail: The provider says it validates profiles against past tenders a customer would have won, but does not establish a user-facing similar-contract feature.

buyerDocuments.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish buyer plans, strategies, minutes, pipelines, budgets or other buyer-authored documents.

buyerRequirements.detail: Match rationales are described, but the reviewed pages do not establish extracted participation conditions, evaluation criteria or recurring buyer requirements.

requirementsPlanning.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish readiness actions, evidence planning or a requirements gap workflow.

awardHistory.detail: The reviewed pages describe live tender opportunities, not historical awards, winners or award search.

frameworks.detail: Example briefs include DPS opportunities, but the reviewed pages do not establish dedicated framework, DPS or dynamic-market discovery or intelligence.

competitorTracking.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish named competitor, incumbent, supplier or winner monitoring.

exportsApi.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish CSV, spreadsheet, API, webhook, CRM or other data export or integration.

collaboration.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish multiple users, assignments, comments or a shared team pipeline.

bidWriting.detail: TenderAI says it finds and scores opportunities for the customer to decide on, but the reviewed pages do not expressly establish or exclude bid-writing functionality.

explicitPortals.detail: Explicitly named as one of the two currently integrated data sources.
Explicitly named as one of the two currently integrated data sources.

otherCoverageClaims.claim: The provider claims the two sources together represent about 100,000 notices per year across the UK public sector, with more sources to be added.

deepAudit.researchSummary: TenderAI sells a low-touch, per-profile email briefing for UK SMEs: two official feeds are scored against a provider-managed business profile and reduced to a short BID/FLAG/SKIP list. The offer is simple and inexpensive to operate, but the public surface gives little evidence of workflow depth, legal maturity, information-security controls or data infrastructure beyond the daily digest.

legalAndMaturity.detail: The reviewed site identifies only the TenderAI brand and brief@tenderai.uk contact, describes 16 active business profiles and a first cohort, and publishes beta-customer testimonials. No registered operator, company number, terms, privacy policy, data-processing terms, physical address or official corporate record was found on the reviewed first-party surface.

targetCustomerAndUseCase.detail: TenderAI explicitly targets UK SMEs without dedicated bid teams across IT, construction, facilities management, consulting, training, health and social care, waste and catering. The intended job is to replace 30-60 minutes of daily manual screening with a two-minute email decision list.

dataSourcesAndCoverageMethod.detail: The current product names exactly two sources: Find a Tender Service and Contracts Finder, aggregated under the Open Government Licence. It claims roughly 100,000 notices per year and broader UK-public-sector coverage, but provides no source inventory beyond those two feeds and no independent completeness evidence.

dataIngestionAndFreshness.detail: The provider says it scans opportunities daily, updates the public digest daily and sends customer briefs each morning, with the first brief at 04:00 UTC after profile setup. It does not publish feed polling intervals, deduplication rules, correction handling, status history, measured ingestion lag or a freshness SLA.

matchingAndQualificationMethod.detail: A concierge-built profile records sector, keywords, sectors served, CPV codes and value range; TenderAI says it validates this profile against past tenders and then applies 0-100 BID, FLAG or SKIP scoring with plain-English rationale. Profile changes are provider-managed by email within 24 hours and self-serve editing is only coming soon.

buyerEntityInvestment.detail: Buyer names appear in tender briefs, but no canonical buyer record, alias handling, duplicate merging, buyer history or cross-notice buyer profile was documented.

supplierEntityInvestment.detail: The personalised business profile is the subscriber's matching configuration, not a supplier-intelligence entity. No winner, incumbent, competitor, alias or cross-award supplier model was found.

renewalSignalMethod.detail: The reviewed pages do not document published contract-end monitoring, calculated expiry windows, extension tracking, predicted re-tender timing or confirmed future-notice linkage.

requirementsPlanningMethod.detail: BID/FLAG/SKIP rationales help triage opportunities, but no requirement extraction, evidence-gap register, owner/action/deadline workflow or readiness state was documented.

historicalAndAwardDepth.detail: TenderAI says it validates a new profile against past tenders the customer would have won, but this is an onboarding method rather than a user-facing history or awards product. No award search, winner/value history, linked notice chain or customer-accessible historical depth was established.

workflowAndIntegrations.detail: The operational surface is an emailed top-ten brief with links to original tender pages and provider-managed profile updates. No CSV/API, CRM or messaging integration, assignments, shared workspace, multi-user controls, comments or tender pipeline was documented.

securitySupportAndOnboarding.detail: Onboarding is a 15-minute call or email exchange, with profile setup promised within hours and ongoing changes by reply email. The reviewed public surface does not state the legal controller, hosting region, authentication model, encryption, retention, sub-processors, tenant isolation, support SLA, security certification or incident route.

commercialModel.detail: The paid offer is £99 per month per business profile with unlimited opportunities, cancel-anytime billing and a free first month; a free weekly digest is also offered. The page says no card is charged for 30 days but does not state clearly whether payment details are required to begin, and no annual, team or enterprise schedule is published.

materialLimitations.detail: Only Find a Tender and Contracts Finder are currently named, leaving devolved and specialist portal coverage unestablished.
No public legal entity, terms, privacy, security or data-processing documentation was found on the reviewed first-party surface.
The product is an email-screening layer with no documented buyer/supplier intelligence, renewals, award history, collaboration, requirements planning or export integration.

contradictions.detail: The homepage says matching is not keyword matching and uses real semantic understanding, while many public daily-digest explanations visibly rely on CPV match, keyword found and value-within-range rules. This may be a hybrid method, but the weighting is not disclosed.
The page calls the offer a free first month and says no card is charged for 30 days, but it does not resolve whether a card is collected at signup.

diligenceQuestions: What legal entity contracts with customers, and where are the terms, privacy policy and data-processing agreement?
Is a payment card required to start the first free month, and what happens automatically on day 30?
How often are each of the two official feeds polled, how are duplicates/corrections handled, and what is measured ingestion latency?
What percentage of the match score comes from semantic analysis versus keywords, CPV codes and value filters?
Can TenderAI provide recall-and-precision results on a representative historical sample for our sector?
What hosting, encryption, retention, access-control and incident-response controls protect company-profile data?

caveats: Provider claims only; Civensa has not independently tested source completeness, semantic scoring or delivery.
The page labels Find a Tender as all UK contracts over £10K and Contracts Finder as MOD plus wider public sector; these characterisations should not be treated as official portal rules.
Self-serve profile editing was described as coming soon; profile changes currently require replying to a brief or emailing the provider.
The page does not clearly state whether a payment card is required to start the free first month, only that no card is charged for 30 days.

providers.name: Tenderlake

pricing.plansText: UK+IE is £325/month on a monthly plan or £249/month paid annually. Europe/UK/Int+ is £546/month on a monthly plan or £396/month paid annually. Bespoke expansions are available by contacting the provider.
pricing.seatDetail: UK+IE includes 2 Primary/Admin and 5 Pro user licences; Europe/UK/Int+ includes 2 Primary/Admin and 7 Pro licences. Additional users are available by discussion; no public extra-seat price is stated.
pricing.vatDetail: VAT treatment is not publicly stated on the reviewed pricing page.
pricing.trialDetail: Seven-day free trial with no credit card required for all listed plans.

comparablePlans.notes: The provider explicitly displays £249/month paid annually; the £2,988 annual total is calculated as £249 × 12 rather than published as a total. VAT treatment is not stated.
The provider explicitly displays £396/month paid annually; the £4,752 annual total is calculated as £396 × 12 rather than published as a total. VAT treatment is not stated.

comparablePlans.includedUsers: Custom; additional users, emails, AI Searches, Keyword Searches and Teams channels are available by discussion
comparablePlans.notes: Custom quote. The pricing FAQ says bespoke plans and invoice payment are available but does not publish currency, billing basis or prices.

semanticAiMatching.detail: Users describe products and services in natural language; Tenderlake evaluates meaning and capability alignment, explains fit and learns from feedback.

buyerProfiles.detail: Buyer procurement profiles aggregate tender history, category mix, similar organisations, awards and suppliers. Tenderlake also models a buyer as a named organisation separate from the multiple aliases users enter to match that buyer across notices, establishing explicit cross-notice identity handling.

supplierProfiles.detail: Users create a canonical contractor organisation with multiple name aliases, then monitor awards to that contractor and analyse competitor award reports across notices. Identity handling is user-configured rather than claimed as automatic.

renewalSignals.detail: Tenderlake shows relevant contracts coming to an end in the next 24 months and alerts on previously awarded contracts nearing expiry.

similarContracts.detail: Notice Similarity Search finds opportunities semantically similar to ideal opportunities or previous wins, across countries and languages.

buyerDocuments.detail: The reviewed pages do not establish buyer plans, strategies, minutes, budgets or other buyer-authored material beyond procurement notices.

buyerRequirements.detail: Capability assessments explain fit and flag potential requirement risks, but the reviewed pages do not establish a normalized register of participation conditions, certifications or recurring buyer requirements.

requirementsPlanning.detail: Qualification workflow is described, but the reviewed pages do not establish evidence-gap, readiness or requirement-by-requirement planning before bid submission.

awardHistory.detail: Plans include more than ten years of history, award update subscriptions and industry contract-awards reports showing winners and other award intelligence.

frameworks.detail: UK+IE explicitly includes frameworks and Dynamic Purchasing Systems.

competitorTracking.detail: Pricing includes competitor tracking, and users can monitor awards to named competitors plus contracts from selected buyers or buyer groups.

exportsApi.detail: Plans include API access; Tenderlake also documents a remote MCP connector for customer-scoped access from AI assistants.

collaboration.detail: Included users can coordinate bid interest, qualification stages and distributions through folders, email lists, Microsoft Teams and Slack channels.

bidWriting.detail: Tenderlake explicitly says it does not write bids and is focused on supplier-side tender intelligence.

explicitPortals.detail: Tenderlake's Find a Tender alternative page explicitly compares its dataset with Find a Tender and says Tenderlake includes UK notices beyond that portal.
Public Tenderlake buyer and notice pages explicitly name and link Contracts Finder records. This demonstrates included records, not a source-wide completeness guarantee.
Public Tenderlake notice pages explicitly link back to Public Contracts Scotland. This demonstrates included records, not a source-wide completeness guarantee.

Public Tenderlake notice pages explicitly link back to Sell2Wales, and the Find a Tender comparison page names Sell2Wales among lower-value UK sources. This does not establish source-wide completeness.

otherCoverageClaims.claim: UK+IE claims lower- and higher-value contracts, including OJEU, across the UK and Ireland. Europe/UK/Int+ adds the UK, EU, Norway, Switzerland, World Bank and other sources, with below-threshold national notices in EU countries.
The product page claims full UK/EU/EEA coverage, 192 countries and more than 200,000 buying organisations; the higher plan claims more than 250,000 buying organisations.

deepAudit.researchSummary: Tenderlake is a mature supplier-side tender-intelligence platform built around multilingual semantic search, workflow distribution, award/contract-end intelligence and cross-notice organisation monitoring. Its strongest defensible depth is the combination of long historical coverage, user-configured buyer/supplier aliasing, sophisticated team routing and current API access, while it intentionally stops before bid writing and detailed requirements planning.

legalAndMaturity.detail: Tenderlake Ltd is an active English private company, number 10295265, incorporated 26 July 2016, with filed accounts through 31 March 2025. The provider terms identify the same company and registered office; a decade-long filing history and current product documentation indicate materially greater operating maturity than launch-stage entrants.

targetCustomerAndUseCase.detail: Tenderlake explicitly serves serious public-sector suppliers, commercial leaders, central tender-intelligence teams and bid operations that need complete UK/EU visibility, faster qualification, multilingual discovery and distribution across business units. Primary/Pro account design also addresses larger workgroups with central administrators and specialist stakeholders.

dataSourcesAndCoverageMethod.detail: The product claims full UK/EU/EEA coverage, coverage in 192 countries and more than 200,000 buying organisations; the higher plan claims more than 250,000. Pricing distinguishes UK+Ireland from a Europe/UK/International tier, and first-party pages explicitly establish TED, Find a Tender, Contracts Finder, Public Contracts Scotland, Sell2Wales and DOS records, but no single exhaustive portal inventory is published.

dataIngestionAndFreshness.detail: Saved searches can feed daily alerts and automatic weekday-morning distributions, while the API lets customers check new or updated procurements using stable identifiers and paging. The reviewed pages do not publish source-specific polling cadences, measured ingestion latency, duplicate/correction rules, a public status history or a contractual freshness SLA.

matchingAndQualificationMethod.detail: Customers describe products, services, scope and exclusions in natural language; Tenderlake evaluates semantic capability alignment, explains relevance and concerns, operates across European languages, and learns from user feedback. Primary users configure shared AI searches while Pro users can maintain personal AI searches; keyword search remains available but is not the core method.

buyerEntityInvestment.detail: Tenderlake provides cross-notice buyer procurement profiles with history, category mix, similar organisations, awards and suppliers. Its monitoring workflow explicitly separates the canonical display organisation from multiple common-name aliases entered to match that buyer across notices; this establishes deliberate identity handling, although the reviewed evidence is user-configured rather than automatic entity resolution.

supplierEntityInvestment.detail: Users create a canonical contractor organisation, attach multiple name aliases and monitor awards across those aliases; award reports aggregate winning suppliers to support competitor, partner and customer analysis. Identity quality depends on the aliases configured by the customer, and no automatic corporate-group resolution claim was found.

renewalSignalMethod.detail: The Contract End Report surfaces previously awarded service and supply contracts whose recorded end dates fall within the next 24 months and alerts users when relevant contracts are nearing expiry. The provider frames this as an opportunity to ask the buyer whether it will re-tender, extend or renew, so the signal is an end-date window rather than confirmation of a future competition.

evidence.label: Contract End Report and renewal feature index

requirementsPlanningMethod.detail: Tenderlake supports relevance explanations, concern flags, qualify-in/out stages and requests from stakeholders to a central team, but no durable requirement-level workflow with evidence gaps, owners, actions, deadlines or readiness state was documented. The provider expressly positions itself as intelligence rather than bid writing.

historicalAndAwardDepth.detail: Published plans include more than ten years of history, award-update subscriptions, industry contract-award reports and contract-end reports. Documentation also describes related-notice chains linking prior information notices, corrections and subsequent awards, and public buyer profiles expose historical tenders, awards and suppliers.

workflowAndIntegrations.detail: Primary administrators configure searches, folders, reports, exports, Teams/Slack connections, email lists and automated distribution; Pro users receive shared folders, submit requests, provide feedback and run personal AI searches. Distribution lists, bid-interest coordination and folder-based routing support larger teams, while the current customer-scoped REST API is versioned and OpenAPI-documented but remains labelled beta.

securitySupportAndOnboarding.detail: The privacy policy says passwords are stored encrypted, connections use SSL and computers/storage are in the UK; API keys are customer-scoped and permissioned. The public offer includes a seven-day no-card trial, demonstrations, Academy tutorials and direct support, but no current sub-processor list, AI data-use boundary, independent certification, penetration-test summary, incident SLA or public status page was found; the privacy policy predates the current AI/API product surface.

commercialModel.detail: UK+Ireland is £325 month-to-month or £249 per month billed annually; Europe/UK/International+ is £546 month-to-month or £396 per month billed annually, with a bespoke tier available. Plans bundle users, AI/keyword searches, alerts, history, renewals, awards, competitor tracking, integrations and API; invoice billing is offered separately at the undiscounted monthly-plan rate.

materialLimitations.detail: Very broad full-coverage and country/organisation claims are not backed by a single exhaustive portal inventory or public source-level freshness metrics.
Buyer and supplier alias handling is explicit but user-configured; automatic entity resolution, corporate-family modelling and duplicate-merge accuracy are not established.
Contract-end alerts indicate expiry risk, not a confirmed extension, renewal or re-tender event.
The service does not write bids and the reviewed workflow does not establish detailed requirement/evidence readiness planning or buyer-authored document intelligence.
The published privacy and terms pages are materially older than current AI, API and connector features and do not disclose a current processor/security assurance package.

contradictions.detail: Pricing presents API access as an included plan feature, while the current API announcement calls it a beta available only to customers on the latest plans and says pricing may evolve after the no-extra-charge beta period.

diligenceQuestions: Provide the exhaustive source inventory, per-source polling cadence, last-90-day ingestion lag and completeness figures.
How much buyer/supplier entity resolution is automatic versus dependent on customer-maintained aliases, and how are reorganisations or corporate groups handled?
Exactly which source field drives Contract End Report dates, how are extension options treated, and are confidence/provenance labels shown?
Which plan/account types can use the API beta, what are its limits, and what pricing or endpoint changes are expected at general availability?
Can Tenderlake supply a current DPA, sub-processor list, AI model/data-use statement, security architecture and independent assurance evidence?
What measured recall and precision does AI Search achieve for our services across the languages and countries we target?

caveats: Provider claims only; Civensa has not independently tested source completeness, AI matching, renewal signals or alert delivery.
The reviewed pages make broad full-coverage claims but do not publish one normalized, exhaustive portal inventory.
The published buyer profiles and example notice links demonstrate records from named portals but do not prove complete ingestion of each source.
Buyer and contractor identity handling uses user-entered aliases on the reviewed feature page; Civensa has not tested automatic entity resolution or duplicate merging.
Annual prices are displayed as monthly equivalents paid annually; invoice billing at the undiscounted monthly-plan rate is described separately.
The provider explicitly says it does not write bids.
